lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - A Listen and say. Then practise.

details: Listen and say develops listening and speaking skills by helping students with model pronunciation by giving them the chance to practise saying the target words or phrases.
Look for careful listening, speaking fluency, confident repetition, and taking turns.
”I’m opening a supermarket. Do you want to be my first customers? What fruit and vegetables do you think I should sell?

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.27 - B. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer develops speaking fluency by allowing students to practise using a simple question and answer format.
Look for pairs using the correct question forms, giving clear answers and taking turns during their short conversations.
“Oh dear! My boxes are all mixed up! Can you ask your partner questions and work together to sort out the fruit and vegetables?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.79 - A Look and circle

details: Look and circle helps students identify target vocabulary by matching the written word with the correct picture.
Look for students scanning pictures carefully, recognising the correct fruit or vegetable and circling the correct items neatly.
“I’ve found a shopping list someone has dropped? Can you help me find everything they are looking for? The only problem is, half of the shopping list seems to be in code!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

Look for accurate letter order and spelling, correct answers and clear writing.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.28 - Speaking Fill Your Cart Circle one fruit and one vegetable. Guess your friends’ fruit and vegetables. Then stick them.

details:
Circle one fruit and one vegetable develops reading recognition and speaking confidence. 

Guess your friends’ fruit and vegetables allows students to practise asking and answering questions to guess classmates’ chosen fruit and vegetables, reinforcing vocabulary and communication skills.
Look for students following instructions, good fluency, taking turns asking and answering and neat bookwork.
“Will you help me at the checkout today? Check what fruit and vegetables your friend is buying to make sure you charge them the right amount!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (closed pairs): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (open pairs): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs
The song provides the opportunity to recognise the target structure and vocabulary in a song as well as practising reading and listening skills.
Look for accurate reading as well as good pronunciation as they follow the lyrics, and finally sing the song as a group.
“You have been so much help in my supermarket!  Let’s sing a song together to celebrate and bring in some new customers!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
